questions.q: Which action will induce a potential difference in a coil of wire? (generator effect)
options: Holding a stationary magnet inside the coil
Moving a magnet into or out of the coil
Placing the coil far from any magnet
Leaving the coil in a steady magnetic field
questions.explain: A potential difference is induced only when there is a change in the magnetic field through the coil, e.g. moving a magnet in or out. A stationary magnet causes no induced p.d.

questions.q: A step-up transformer has more turns on the secondary coil than the primary. What does it do to the potential difference?
questions.explain: In a step-up transformer np < ns, so by Vp/Vs = np/ns the secondary (output) p.d. is greater than the primary. The current is correspondingly smaller.

questions.q: What is the key difference between an alternator and a dynamo?
options: An alternator produces direct current (dc); a dynamo produces alternating current (ac)
An alternator uses slip rings and produces ac; a dynamo uses a split-ring commutator and produces dc
They are identical in every way
questions.explain: An alternator uses slip rings, giving alternating current (ac). A dynamo uses a split-ring commutator, which reverses the connections each half turn to give direct current (dc).

questions.q: A transformer has 100 turns on the primary and 500 turns on the secondary. The primary p.d. is 12 V. Calculate the secondary p.d.
questions.explain: Vp/Vs = np/ns, so Vs = Vp × ns/np = 12 × 500/100 = 60 V. This is a step-up transformer.

questions.q: How can you increase the size of the induced potential difference from a generator?
options: Move the magnet or coil more slowly
Use fewer turns on the coil
Move the magnet faster, use more turns, or use a stronger magnet
questions.explain: A larger induced p.d. results from a faster rate of change of the field, more turns on the coil, or a stronger magnet — all increase how quickly field lines are cut.

questions.q: A transformer has 800 turns on the primary and 200 turns on the secondary. The primary p.d. is 230 V. Calculate the secondary p.d.
questions.explain: Vp/Vs = np/ns, so Vs = Vp × ns/np = 230 × 200/800 = 57.5 V. This is a step-down transformer.

questions.q: A 100% efficient transformer has a primary p.d. of 230 V and primary current of 2.0 A. The secondary p.d. is 23 V. Calculate the secondary current.
questions.explain: For an ideal transformer VpIp = VsIs, so Is = VpIp/Vs = (230 × 2.0)/23 = 460/23 = 20 A.

questions.q: Why does the national grid use step-up transformers before transmission over long distances?
options: To increase the current and reduce the voltage
To increase the voltage and reduce the current, which reduces energy lost as heat in the cables
To convert ac to dc for transmission
questions.explain: Stepping up the p.d. reduces the current for the same power (P = VI). Lower current means much less energy wasted as heat in the resistance of the transmission cables (heating ∝ I²R).

questions.q: In a moving-coil microphone, what causes the electrical signal to be generated?
options: Sound waves move a coil near a magnet, inducing a changing p.d.
questions.explain: In a microphone, sound waves make a diaphragm and attached coil vibrate near a magnet. The changing magnetic field through the moving coil induces an alternating p.d. — the generator effect — which matches the sound.

questions.q: What happens to the induced potential difference if the direction in which a magnet moves through a coil is reversed?
questions.explain: Reversing the motion (or the magnet's poles) reverses the direction of the induced p.d. This is why a coil rotating in a field produces alternating current.

questions.q: A coil rotates steadily in a magnetic field. At which position is the induced p.d. greatest?
options: When the coil is parallel to the field lines, cutting them fastest
When the coil is perpendicular to the field lines
questions.explain: The induced p.d. is largest when the coil cuts field lines at the greatest rate. This occurs as the coil moves parallel to the field lines, and is zero when it momentarily moves along the lines without cutting them.

questions.q: Why must a transformer use an alternating current in the primary coil?
options: To keep the iron core cool
To create a continuously changing magnetic field that induces a p.d. in the secondary
questions.explain: A transformer works only with a changing magnetic field. Alternating current produces a continually changing field in the iron core, which induces an alternating p.d. in the secondary coil. A steady dc would give no induced p.d. after switch-on.

questions.q: A transformer has 240 turns on the primary and 1200 turns on the secondary. The primary p.d. is 25 V. Calculate the secondary p.d.
questions.explain: Vp/Vs = np/ns, so Vs = Vp × ns/np = 25 × 1200/240 = 25 × 5 = 125 V (a step-up transformer).

questions.q: A step-down transformer reduces 230 V to 11.5 V. The primary coil has 4000 turns. How many turns are on the secondary coil?
An ideal transformer has an input power of 60 W. If it is 100% efficient, what is the output power?
questions.explain: For an ideal (100% efficient) transformer, output power equals input power, so VsIs = VpIp = 60 W. No energy is lost.

questions.q: A 100% efficient transformer has a secondary p.d. of 400 000 V and a secondary current of 50 A. If the primary p.d. is 25 000 V, calculate the primary current.
questions.explain: For an ideal transformer VpIp = VsIs, so Ip = VsIs/Vp = (400000 × 50)/25000 = 20 000 000/25 000 = 800 A.

questions.q: In the national grid, what is the role of a step-down transformer near homes?
options: To raise the voltage for long-distance transmission
To lower the voltage to a safer level for domestic use
To increase the current in the transmission lines
questions.explain: Step-up transformers raise the voltage for efficient transmission; step-down transformers near towns and homes lower the voltage (e.g. to 230 V) so it is safe to use in buildings.

questions.q: Which device uses a split-ring commutator to produce direct current as a coil rotates?
questions.explain: A dc dynamo (generator) uses a split-ring commutator, which swaps the coil's connections every half turn so the output current always flows the same way — direct current. An alternator uses slip rings and gives ac.
